about: Readouts with the digits their source supports. Expected values are worked by hand from the timebase and the ticks; the period rows' edges are identify-swd's SWDIO and SWCLK around the first DPIDR read.

tests.name: tickPlace: the largest power of ten not above one tick

rows.note: 1 ns
10 us
5 us: 1 us is the largest power below
3 s ticks: 1 s

tests.name: formatInterval: digits down to the tick and no further

rows.note: The brief's own example: at 1 ns, 1.234567 ms, never 1.2345670 ms.
A trailing zero at the ns digit is a measured digit and stays.
123 ticks of 10 us is 1.23 ms.
247 ticks of 5 us is 1.235 ms, exact at the us digit.
4 ticks at 3 MS/s is 1.333... us; the tick is 333 ns, so the last digit is 100 ns. One digit more (1.33 us) or fewer (1 us) is the off-by-one this row catches.

tests.name: formatRate: digits from a span uncertain by about one tick

rows.note: One 40 ns period: 25 MHz, uncertain by 25 MHz / 40 = 625 kHz, so the last digit is 100 kHz. Rounding the place up instead of down would print 25 MHz.
1000 periods over 40000 ticks: 25 MHz, uncertain by 625 Hz: last digit 100 Hz.
One 1 us period: 1 MHz, uncertain by exactly 1 kHz, a power of ten: last digit 1 kHz. A "smaller than" rule instead of "not larger than" would print 1.0000 MHz.
45 periods over 45016 ticks: 999,644.57 Hz, uncertain by 22.2 Hz: to 10 Hz, 999,640 Hz.

tests.name: periodStats: rising edge to rising edge, starting low

rows.note: SWDIO, low before the first edge. Rising at 377094556, 377096556, 377099556, 377101556, 377106074: periods 2000, 3000, 2000, 4518. Sorted 2000, 2000, 3000, 4518; the lower middle is 2000 (the mean of the middle two, 2500, did not occur). Falling-to-falling would give three periods with a maximum of 3522; counting edges would give 9 or 8. Tukey's fences: Q1 = p[0] = 2000, Q3 = p[3] = 4518, IQR 2518; all four inside, one run of 11518 ticks.

tests.name: periodStats: starting high, the first edge falls

rows.note: The same SWDIO from its second edge, high before it. Rising at 377096556, 377099556, 377101556, 377106074: periods 3000, 2000, 4518, all inside the fences (Q1 2000, Q3 4518). Taking the first edge as rising measures the falling edges instead: 2000, 3000, 3522.

tests.name: periodStats: SWCLK at 1 MHz, and fewer than two rising edges
Tukey's fences: the Escapement session's 50 MHz request keeps all seven periods

rows.note: Periods 19, 22, 17, 22, 20, 19, 22 ns (wire_swd/request/380567191 in gcc-swd-reads), each high for half its period, from tick 1000. Sorted 17 19 19 20 22 22 22: Q1 = p[1] = 19, Q3 = p[5] = 22, IQR 3, fences [14.5, 26.5]. All seven, one run of 141 ticks: 7 / 141 ns = 49.645 MHz, uncertain by 1/141 of it, 352 kHz: 49.6 MHz. The one-tick window keeps 20, 19, 19 in two runs, 58 ticks, and reads 52 MHz.

tests.name: Tukey's fences: one 80 ns period among 27 ns ones is dropped

rows.note: 27 ×5, 80, 27 ×5. Sorted, Q1 = p[2] = 27, Q3 = p[8] = 27, IQR 1 (the floor): fences [25.5, 28.5]. Ten kept, in two runs of 135: 10 / 270 ns = 37.04 MHz, uncertain by 2/270 of it, 274 kHz: 37.0 MHz.

tests.name: Tukey's fences: the IQR is at least one tick, so a tick of jitter stays

rows.note: 27 ×5, 28, 27 ×5: Q1 = Q3 = 27. With IQR 0 the fences would be [27, 27] and drop the 28; at one tick they are [25.5, 28.5]. All 11 kept, 298 ticks: 36.91 MHz, uncertain by 1/298, 124 kHz: 36.9 MHz.

tests.name: Tukey's fences: Q3 is p[⌈3(n − 1)/4⌉], not the floor

rows.note: Six periods, sorted 20 20 20 20 30 50: Q1 = p[1] = 20, Q3 = p[⌈3.75⌉] = p[4] = 30, IQR 10, fences [5, 45]: the 30 stays, the 50 goes. Q3 = p[3] = 20 would give IQR 1 and drop the 30.

tests.name: Tukey's fences: 93 and 100 ns alternating are both kept

rows.note: Sorted 93 ×4, 100 ×4: Q1 = p[1] = 93, Q3 = p[6] = 100, IQR 7, fences [82.5, 110.5]. All eight, one run of 772 ticks: 8 / 772 ns = 10.3627 MHz, uncertain by 1/772, 13.4 kHz: 10.36 MHz. The one-tick window around the median (93) keeps only the 93s.

tests.name: Tukey's fences: a 33 and a 34 ns stretch among 27 ns periods are both dropped

rows.note: 27 27 27 33 27 27 27 34 27 27 27 27. Sorted, Q1 = p[2] = 27, Q3 = p[9] = 27, IQR 1, fences [25.5, 28.5]: both stretches out. A window of 25 % around the median, [20.25, 33.75], would keep the 33 and drop the 34. Ten kept in three runs, 270 ticks: 37.04 MHz, uncertain by 3/270 of it, 412 kHz: 37.0 MHz.

tests.name: the running clock: a quantised 26.67 ns clock

rows.note: A 26.67 ns clock sampled at 1 ns reads as 26 ns ten times and 27 ns twenty-two times, here 27, 27, 26 over and over. The median is 27 ns (37.04 MHz). Sorted, Q1 = p[7] = 26 and Q3 = p[24] = 27, IQR 1, fences [24.5, 28.5]: all 32 periods inside, one run of 854 ticks: 32 / 854 ns is 37,470,726 Hz, uncertain by 1/854 of that, 43.9 kHz, so to 10 kHz: 37.47 MHz. The mean period, 854 / 32 = 26.6875 ns, is uncertain by 1/32 ns: to 0.01 ns, 26.69 ns.

tests.name: the running clock: a span with a gap between bursts

rows.note: Real SWCLK: the end of the DPIDR read's burst and the start of the next transfer's. Periods 1000 four times, the 90,918-tick gap, then 1000 four times. First-to-last would be 9 periods over 98,918 ticks, 90.98 kHz. Q1 = Q3 = 1000, IQR 1, fences [998.5, 1001.5]: the running clock takes the eight 1000s, two runs of 8000 ticks in all: 1 MHz, uncertain by 2/8000 of it, 250 Hz, so to 100 Hz. Its period, 1000 ticks, is uncertain by 2/8 of a tick: to 0.1 ns.

tests.name: formatValue: to the digit of one code step

rows.note: verge's energy capture: integer mV, read as V; the value is 3305 * 0.001 in f64.
integer nA, read as A: 32898465 nA is 32.898465 mA; the value is 32898465 * 1e-9 in f64.
An f32 source states no resolution: four significant digits. 0.00012345 A rounds half away from zero to 123.5 uA.

tests.name: formatValue: to `significant` figures where the channel states them, if coarser than a step

rows.note: verge's current: a step of 1 nA, but the reading carries four figures, so 350,123,456 nA reads to 0.1 mA.
1,234 nA: four figures end at 1 nA, the step.
12 nA: four figures would go past the step, so the step wins.
Zero has no figures to count: it keeps to the step. The test compared this with the next row's call; both are written out here.
A float channel stating six figures: 123.45 uA to 1 nA.

tests.name: formatBrief: three significant figures for a summary line, never finer than a tick

rows.note: 999.6 ms rounds up into the next unit, still three figures: 1.00 s, not 1000 ms.
15 ticks of 1 ns: 15 ns, not 15.0 ns.
3 ticks of 10 us: 30 us.

tests.name: the running clock's count: one period, one of several, a mean of the rest

rows.note: A single 79 ns period: "79 ns, one period", not "mean of 1 periods".
